story_a.qn1: Do I admit to my boss that I made a mistake, or should I keep my mouth shut for once?
story_a.qn2: How much will I receive as refund if I return one of the shoes?
story_a.narrative: I'm a sales rep for a certain company. I was taking to someone I met online (but haven't yet met in person) about my job. They jokingly asked me if I was able to give them a friends and family discount, and I admitted I could. To make matters worse, I actually shared the specifics of said discount (how much/for how long). Immediately after I told them, it dawned on me that I should have kept my mouth shut. Now I am freaking out about what to do. Yes,  I'm stupid, I know.

I shared the specifics of the discount (how much and for how long).

story_b.qn2: How to we tell my aunt that dad doesn't want a visit from her?
story_b.narrative: We are starting hospice and there is a family member who has had a contentious relationship at best over the years that will probably want to visit during very soon. The issue is that dad doesn't want a visit from his sister and we just aren't quite sure how to deliver this news. We just found out that hospice is starting today and are delivering the news to family. We just aren't sure how to tell my aunt that he doesn't want a visit from her. They have never been that close over the years. During this time that we are telling one sister not to come the other sister is coming.
events: They found out that hospice is starting today.

story_a.qn1: Does anyone know a good studie for me?
story_a.qn2: Can someone help me with an independent study for school?
story_a.narrative: Hey everyone! I'm a 21 year old who's working atm. I'm doing something that doesn't pay much and isn't seen as a high quality job. The last few months I was thinking of going to college and try and get a diplom. Not only so that I can do something I want to do and gain more money, but other reasons to. For example, when I have children I want to help them out when they go to college, and know what they are going trough, and tell them that I've gone trough the same. The only problem is that I don't know what to study. I've checked things, but I can't find a right one. I'm a guy that doesn't have many interests and if I do, it'll be something that has only a 5% chance of being able to live on the money you get from it. My interests are: - Sports - Music (I play guitar) - and the health of the human body - Writing - Gaming  In highshool I was good at Sports, music (of course), english... but not at geographics or french.
events: I was thinking of going to college and getting a diploma over the last few months.
I checked various options for what to study.

story_b.qn1: why is it hard to fit-in in America?
story_b.qn2: Why would my parents change my date of birth?
story_b.narrative: I was born and raised in a developing country. Using family money and being good in math & science, I was able to move to the US and get an education and a successful career. Problem is, I am not able to break in the "high society". I don't get invited to private parties or weekend getaways or friendly retreats. I have tried hobbies, interest groups, meet ups, you name it. Most friends I make turn out to be other "misfits" wanting exactly the same thing- so we cannot really help each other out. I can only think of the following reasons:  1 - Some immigrants have cultural/religious baggage that keeps them from melting in the host society. This does not apply to me since I have always thought of myself as a modern, secular, freethinking individual. 2 - Some immigrants due to the hardships growing up, stick to a minimalist, frugal lifestyle even after they become successful, which reflects in their hygiene, style, and activities they are willing to partake, and this obviously affects their social circle. This is not me either since I was born in a fairly affluent environment and use my money to live better. In summary, I work, pay taxes, consume, go to bars/restaurants, but that's pretty much it. I am not part of the american social life going on behind closed doors.
events: I was born in a developing country.
I moved to the US.
I got an education.
I got a successful career.
I tried hobbies, interest groups, and meet ups.

story_a.qn1: What should I be when I grow up?
story_a.qn2: Is there certificates or classes I should try to do on the side?
story_a.narrative: I am about to finish my degree in biology(I'm a veteran so I started a bit late, I'm 29 now). I'm currently working as a lab tech at an environmental lab but the entire reason I chose to get my BS in Biology was I wanted to work at a zoo or with animals in some way. Every time I see a keeper job posted they want experience of 1-3 years with whatever type of animal that may be. I work full-time now and go to school at night, my schedule is very full. I am not scared of hard work but I just don't understand what path I should venture on to get to this goal. Any help to point me in the right direction would be very awesome. Thanks! Also, wanted to add that I understand there are internships but I have a family (wife and child) to support. I would take a pay cut for experience but I couldn't work for free.
events: I started my degree later than typical
I chose to pursue a BS in Biology
I am about to finish my degree in biology

story_b.qn1: Should I leave my full-time bank job to work retail part-time and go back to school full time?
story_b.qn2: Would there be any way to get a raise without mentioning about new teller's salary?
story_b.narrative: I have been a part time bank teller at a bank here in Maryland. I was recently promoted to a float (working in different branches as needed) full time teller after being with my employer for eight months without getting a raise. I was even told during my initial interview that I will be given a raise after a performance review on my 6th month which never happened. I had to temporarily train two new tellers in a brand-new branch that opened up. One of the new teller and I ended up talking about our pay. She mentioned that her rate is at $12.50, while mine is only at $12. I have nothing against her, but I am a bit infuriated at my employer as I had to wait eight months, as a part-timer, to get a full-time position as there were no full-time positions available then and still only earning $12. Meanwhile, she is automatically a full-timer w/o experience at her hired date. I just feel it's unfair that they've taken advantage of my naivety when I first interviewed with them only because I didn't know how much tellers are actually getting paid. TD;LR New bank teller paid .50 higher than me.
events: I was told during my initial interview that I would be given a raise after a performance review on my 6th month
The promised raise never happened
I was recently promoted to a float full time teller
I temporarily trained two new tellers in a brand-new branch
I talked about pay with one of the new tellers
She mentioned that her rate is $12.50 while mine is $12

story_b.qn2: Do I say anything to my boss?
story_b.narrative: Had an incident this weekend that really upset me and I feel I was screwed over . Where I work it was a blackout weekend ,meaning we had to work based on how busy we would be. I am a manager running a successful business and am always there when things are the busiest. A couple weeks ago I asked my district leader if there was any way I could possibly get Sunday off .He asked why and I was honest and told them it was the last time I'd see my sister for awhile as she is moving to New York .It was her birthday and she was having a big party in the morning . My sister is 8 by the way that is why it was a morning thing . My boss said " no I really need you there but I'll let you leave at 5" . I fought it and told him the party was in the morning and let him know how important it was to me and my family. There was no budging or comprise . My first thought was don't tell them and my second thought was they probably wouldn't care . Never the less I  worked on Sunday . What put me over the edge and made me want to get advice was towards the end of my full shift I decided to dig into some schedules from within our little district and found out that 2 managers had been scheduled off for the day . Another manager had only a 5-9 shift. I was told no!!!

Boss said he needed me but would let me leave at 5
Fought and told him the party was in the morning and how important it was
Worked on Sunday

story_a.qn1: Any support available that would help us with this?
story_a.qn2: Can I afford to have a child?
story_a.narrative: I'm a 32/f on a stable relationship. Me and my partner work very hard but our combined salaries come to just about 55,000. We live in London which is a very expensive city, rent our home (a 2-bedroom flat) and don't have a car. We would really like to have a child but I don't want to be called irresponsible for doing so on a low-ish income. I can't afford private education like my sister can with her kids, and neither my partner or I have any family around us to support us. I have all the will power and love in the world, but I want to know what you guys think.
events: They rent their 2-bedroom flat in London.

story_b.qn1: What is the best response when someone technically above you asks you "What's going on?
story_b.qn2: Should I ask for a pay raise?
story_b.narrative: I've been with the company for about 4 months now and I'm an administrative assistant. My company has given me much more work then what is in my original job description (taking over key tasks to other employee's jobs). I have always volunteered to take on any job no matter what it is. I constantly hear other employees saying "if we hire college students, we won't have to pay them as much as a normal employee." I just graduated from college so this makes me very uncomfortable. I'm constantly worn out from the tasks that I have taken on and it is well known that my boss is ridiculously cheap. I'm unsure how much value or worth the company sees in me even though I work extremely hard. Also, I calculated that if I was paying my tuition with my hourly rate excluding taxes and spending a cent of it, it would take me 10 years to pay off my college loans without taking interest rates into consideration. I really just need some advice.
events: Graduated from college.
Joined the company as an administrative assistant four months ago.
Company gave the narrator much more work than the original job description, taking over key tasks from other employees.
Calculated that paying tuition with hourly rate would take ten years to pay off college loans.
